skill.name: operating-k8s-local
skill.description: Guide local Kubernetes development with Minikube, kubectl, local Docker image builds, service access, and basic troubleshooting.
skill.summary: Use Minikube and kubectl to run, deploy, and debug local Kubernetes workloads.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: The skill is an instructional local Kubernetes guide and does not contain executable installation hooks or prompt injection. Most static findings are Markdown command examples or local Kubernetes workflows, but one sudo hosts-file edit is a real elevated-permission risk. The guide also includes literal Kubernetes Secret examples that should be made safer for users.

remediation.suggestion: Replace the sudo hosts-file command with port forwarding or Minikube service access when possible. If hosts-file editing remains, add a warning, user confirmation, and cleanup steps.
Mark Secret values as placeholders and recommend secure local secret handling. Avoid commands that place real credentials in shell history.

remediation.issue: Local command examples can affect the wrong cluster
remediation.suggestion: Add a reminder to verify the active kubectl context before applying manifests, editing resources, or running debug commands.

content.value_statement: Local Kubernetes setup can be slow when cluster, image, and service steps are scattered. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code concise Minikube and kubectl workflows.
actual_capabilities: Start, stop, delete, and switch Minikube clusters with common resource settings.
Enable Minikube addons such as ingress, metrics-server, dashboard, and storage-provisioner.
Build local Docker images and configure Minikube image usage.
Apply kubectl commands for contexts, pods, logs, rollouts, scaling, and port forwarding.
Provide example Deployment, Service, ConfigMap, Secret, and Ingress manifests.
Debug local pods, service DNS, resource usage, and crash logs.
limitations: It is focused on local Minikube clusters, not managed cloud Kubernetes services.
Commands are examples and may need changes for your operating system or driver.
It does not replace Kubernetes security review for production workloads.
It does not automate cluster setup without user approval.

use_cases.title: Set up a local cluster
use_cases.description: A backend developer starts Minikube, enables addons, and deploys a service for local testing.

use_cases.title: Debug a failing pod
use_cases.description: A platform engineer checks pod events, previous logs, service DNS, and resource usage in a local namespace.

use_cases.title: Prepare Kubernetes manifests
use_cases.description: A DevOps learner builds basic Deployment, Service, ConfigMap, Secret, and Ingress files for practice.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Minikube cluster
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me start a local Minikube cluster for a small web app. Include resource settings, useful addons, and status checks.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy a local image
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through building a Docker image into Minikube and deploying it with imagePullPolicy set for local use.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot a local service
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me diagnose why my local Kubernetes service is not reachable. Ask for context, then suggest kubectl and Minikube checks.

prompt_templates.title: Review a local workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my local Kubernetes workflow for Minikube. Identify risky steps, missing cleanup, and safer alternatives for secrets and host changes.

output_examples.input: I need to run my API locally on Kubernetes.
output: Start Minikube with clear resource settings.
Enable ingress and metrics-server when needed.
Build the local image inside Minikube.
Deploy manifests and verify pods, services, and logs.

output_examples.input: My pod keeps restarting in Minikube.
output: Confirm image availability and pull policy.
Inspect resource usage and readiness probe settings.

output_examples.input: I need local ingress for my app.
output: Confirm the service selector and target port.
Avoid privileged host-file edits unless clearly required.

best_practices: Confirm the active kubectl context before applying or editing resources.
Use placeholder secrets only in examples, and keep real credentials out of shell history and source control.
Prefer port forwarding or Minikube service URLs before changing privileged host files.
anti_patterns: Running privileged host-file changes without explaining why they are needed.
Copying sample Secret values into real manifests or repositories.
Applying manifests to the current context without checking that it is Minikube.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code guide local Kubernetes work with Minikube and kubectl.

faq.question: Does it manage cloud clusters?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on local Minikube workflows. Use a cloud Kubernetes skill for managed clusters.

faq.question: Can it help with local Docker images?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to build images for Minikube and set image pull behavior for local testing.

faq.question: Does it execute commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides command guidance. Users should review commands before running them.

faq.question: Are the Secret examples production ready?
faq.answer: No. They are placeholders. Use a secure secret workflow for real credentials.

faq.question: What tools does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Minikube, kubectl, Docker image workflows, Kubernetes manifests, service access, and basic debugging.
